steps.text: Once upon the land, there was no meaning in looking up.
There was nothing worth looking at up there, nothing worth exploring. That place was the domain of those who indulged in fantasies, those with their heads in the clouds.
But now, each and every person lifts their heads, looking up at the beam of light connecting heaven and earth.
Looking up at the once untouchable sky.
Among the stars, within the artificial constructs that appear so small before the torrent of light, brews the human ambition of this current epoch.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Kristen, Kristen...

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Sure enough, you set this plan into motion a long time ago. Everything you did for the DOD was a fancy show.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Hah! What's the principle behind all this? The efficiency and stability of this high-energy confinement field... I've never heard of anything like that before.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: If I recall correctly, you boasted that you were the foremost expert in high energy physics when you joined Rhine.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: ...One of the foremost experts.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: My God...

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You should thank your lucky stars, Saria, that there's nobody like Kristen in your field.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: It's just not fair. And yet she... she doesn't even bother to publish these results.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The H.A.M.H.R.R. is currently charging.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: According to the military's Horizon Arc Project, once the charging phase is complete, all of this energy will be focused and undergo excitation a second time to deliver powerful wide-area strikes.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Sure. How much longer will it take?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Kristen turned the project dossiers into scrap paper... All I can say is, it won't be long now.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: This is our last chance to stop it.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: As well as our last chance to stop her.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What are you still standing around slack-jawed for, Ferdinand? Time isn't on our side.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Saria, take a look at the densitometer over there.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The needle seems to be fluctuating a lot.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: No, I'm not talking about the needle. The wobbling is a normal phenomenon of high-energy confinement fields. I'm talking about... the unit of measurement.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You can take a guess how many times larger this unit is than the one on the instruments in my lab.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The energy it absorbed just now is enough to power every single one of Columbia's nomadic cities for at least six months.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And it's showing no signs of stopping.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And we're now in the center of the laboratory carrying this tremendous amount of energy.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Even if Nasti is a genius, she can't create a receptacle that stores energy in amounts beyond the realm of cognition.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: In other words–

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: No matter what direction it ultimately focuses the energy in, once the second-degree excitation begins, this lab won't be safe from the consequences.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Her end goal has never changed.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: If her ultimate goal is the sky, and the sky can only be contested with this amount of energy...

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What exactly is up there?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: That's none of my concern.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: All I know is, this is a reckless experiment.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And it's doomed to fail.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Saria, there's nothing stopping you from packing your bags, finding a nice hillside with a great view, and enjoying a drink while you watch this fireworks show that may well go down in the annals of Columbian history.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: That isn't going to happen.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What about you? You were never the risk-taking type.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Looks like my old friends are coming, and they'll be here sooner than expected.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You're right though. I'm not taking any chances. The technical manual has the location of the escape pod, and I know where it is.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'm not particularly interested in seeing the one who fired me, and it's not like you need my help.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: An opportunity to document high energy physics phenomena of this magnitude is rare, and I don't intend to pass it up. Maybe you'll see a new paper from me in the journals next quarter.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I promise, it'll be era-defining.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Unlike Kristen, I don't tie all my intellect to my personal grievances.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The fact that she's consigning all this knowledge to the grave, knowledge that could transform Terra's entire academic landscape... That's something I can't abide.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Do what you need to do, Saria. We don't have much time.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Stay safe.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Ferdinand.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: It's been a while, Colonel.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I'm not surprised you survived, but if I were in your shoes, I'd pretend to be dead.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Get the hell out of Dodge. Go to Victoria or Leithanien. With your skills, you can always pick up a teaching job.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I didn't expect to hear those words coming from you.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Let me say this one more time, Ferdinand: It's over.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I've already spoken with the Vice President. The DOD's defeat is absolute.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: As for whether or not this whole situation can be salvaged, or who controls my fate, I actually don't care that much anymore.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Let's save some dignity for each other, Ferdinand. Get out of here, and I'll save a crossbow bolt for myself.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Huh, what was that? Sorry, my mind wandered for a second there.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Also, you're blocking the radiometer display.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This S.H.A.F.T. here runs a lot deeper than I expected...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm afraid the military simply failed to fully understand its structure.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Right here... is where the Transmitter's response is the strongest.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You...
What are you doing here, Silence?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Professor... Parvis...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Silence... The location of this lab is supposed to be top secret. How did you manage to find your way here?
Silence tries hard to open her eyes wide, discerning the things in the room.
In the corner of the room, an instrument is humming as if breathing. A Transmitter sits in a transparent tank, bobbing up and down. Across the room are several books with black covers.
As if sensing Silence's presence, the Transmitter increases its activity. A strong wave of dizziness makes Silence furrow her brow and shake her head a few times.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Ah, that's right. You have your own Transmitter...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Hmm, these reactive tendencies... You injected yourself with the Transmitter? Though, I'm not surprised.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Does it cause you occasional discomfort?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: An entirely normal response. I also have it inside my body. It can be quite overwhelming for an old man like myself, but it shouldn't be a problem for you youths.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Still, this is the only way to better control the reaction process.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Don't worry. Once this experiment is over, the long-distance intertwining properties of this batch of Transmitter will be lost, and they won't affect the long-term health of the injected.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What experiment? You're conducting an experiment here?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Silence, did you hurt your hand?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Does it get in the way of your work?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Then I won't ask any more questions. Now is the most critical moment.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: That you've found your way here... might just be the help I've needed.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I was just complaining how much easier the data processing would be if you were here.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Lately, I... Actually, never mind.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Tell me, what kind of experiment are you running?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: There has only ever been one area of research I've fully dedicated my energy to.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Chimerism.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Precisely. This is the last question to be answered in chimera research.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But, this is...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Professor, what are all these documents? The text on them seems...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Quite 'evil,' right? This is an ancient Sarkaz tome that records the 'history' of a certain ethnic branch.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: That Sarkaz branch not only enjoys long lifespans, but can even transcend the shackles of physical form and exist in the world in a purely spiritual state.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: They have been dubbed, the 'revenants.' The pronunciation can be a bit esoteric, but I'm sure you'll be able to find some records in Victorian.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Silence, have you ever considered what chimerism does at the level of the soul?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: A soul chimera?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: These 'revenants,' the so-called 'soul' in ancient Originium Arts and Sarkaz witchcraft, can they be produced a posteriori?

spans.text: These 'revenants,' the so-called 'soul' in ancient Originium Arts and Sarkaz witchcraft, can they be produced

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Are you trying to create an artificial consciousness?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You've always been my finest student.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: This is something I've been working on for decades, to little avail. That is, until Ferdinand told me that he and Dorothy had jointly produced this particular 'Transmitter.'

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You can't begin to imagine how excited I was, Silence!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I was absolutely sure that the properties of the 'Transmitter'... were sufficient to form the soil from which artificial consciousness could be born.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: However, in this land, disturbances will always exist no matter how sophisticated the lab is. These disturbances have plagued me for the longest time...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: There are so many possibilities. Perhaps the energy used to excite the Transmitter was insufficient, perhaps the laboratory was not sealed off enough, perhaps Originium interferes with the generation and aggregation of consciousness.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But, none of that matters anymore. All mysteries will finally be unraveled today.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: This will be my final research project.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: The most optimal research environment is about to take shape.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Professor Parvis, you were responsible for using Transmitter to solve Arc-01's accuracy control problem. This is... the new Transmitter core.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Kristen wanted to do something she saw as taking a risk. She thought her work to be meaningful... I hate to be a critic of my peer's efforts, but let's be honest: we researchers have been cowards for far too long.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Mediocrity, boredom, risk-aversion, indecisiveness... Silence, those of us with the knowledge and ability have to do more than just 'explore' or 'progress.'

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: We carry science upon our shoulders, are commanded by it, are driven by it. It requires us to take on responsibilities that only a strong soul can endure.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: ––Usher in a new era.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...'Usher in a new era'?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Silence... You deserve to be here with me to witness this crowning achievement.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Soon, very soon now... the dark ages of mediocrity will come to an end, and the pantheon of science must return.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're shaking all over. I've rarely seen you like this.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Is that so? Perhaps the Transmitter's reaction is getting a bit too intense. Maybe I really am getting too old.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I'm sure you can relate with me, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes, I can.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I can see you've really been looking forward to this moment.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Then, there's one thing I have to make clear. I will destroy this Transmitter core.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I mean, I'm putting a stop to everything that's happening here.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Whether it's Control's plan or just your personal ambitions, all of this has to be reexamined.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's what I'm here for.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: That girl shook your allegiance to science, but I've always believed that you had the makings of a researcher.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: And as such, I never really blamed you.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But this time, whether or not this is some ridiculous joke, I'm not going to stand for it.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I'll have you apologize to me, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I won't take back a single word I said, Professor.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I don't think I've done anything wrong, be it back then or now. What you people are really after is wanton power.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: That's absurd. You couldn't be more wrong, Silence.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: That's right. Say what you will about me craving power. Because I know what kind of research is important, and what kind of research can shape the future.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: What, are you going to regurgitate that old platitude about science belonging to the masses?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Let me tell you, Silence, that science belongs to the Übermenschen. The supermen.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: The mediocre can go elect their politicians and kiss the feet of their betters...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But only science is above their meddling.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What about you then? Are you part of the 'Übermenschen' you aspire to?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: ...That ship has already sailed for me.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But if the consciousness I create is rational enough, grand enough, then it can––

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It can't, Professor.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If you don't even have faith in humanity, what makes you think that this nascent consciousness can supersede everything?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You don't understand.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You've poured your heart and soul into the field of chimeric research, attempting time after time to craft powerful creations through bioengineering. Is that all because...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You can't run from your own weakness?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: ...Silence, I won't allow you to throw baseless speculation around like that.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: This is... my last hope to break free from mediocrity.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...I didn't expect to see you here.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: My former Defense colleagues.
That's right, Director Saria. 'Former colleagues.'
We are now employees of Components Control Section.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: 'Components Control.'

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: You aren't allowed past this point.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You're doing a better job than last time.

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: I appreciate the sentiment.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You all know what Kristen is trying to do. All this accomplishes is–

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: I don't know, and I don't particularly care.

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: You know my ID number from Rhine, Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: 011. That was before Jara came. Kristen and I interviewed you, James.

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: Back then, I had offers from other companies, including Volvort Kochinski and Beachbrella. But, I didn't give them a second thought.

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: Because I always believed in you. You and Kristen. I believed you two were different from the rest of them.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: That was just your ego speaking, James. This whole place is about to crash. I'd recommend you hurry up and grab an escape pod.

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: I'll wait here until the moment we crash.

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: But before that, want to see something spectacular, Saria?

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: Nasti described it to us...
Saria notices the entire corridor shifting.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Is that—

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: I've never seen the land from this high up before.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The H.A.M.H.R.R. has begun altitude adjustment.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Out of the way! There's no time!

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Dammit, what's going on?! This blasted thing's spinning?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: If I had to guess, this would be the 'altitude adjustment' mentioned in the technical manual, which is the step right before secondary excitation.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Sir, do you need my help?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Why are these doors in the corridor shut? Where's Ferdinand?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: He slipped away just now–

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Go after him!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Are there no defense systems here other than the partition doors in the corridor?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: If I had any say in it, this place would be stuffed full of power armor.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Freeze, Ferdinand.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Got you.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I need you to leave me alone, Colonel. Every minute here is precious.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And dealing with you would waste all my energy.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I thought we were peas in a pod, Ferdinand. Sober rationalists who would weigh the pros and cons before making a decision.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Looks like I had the wrong read on you.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Come with us.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The beam excitation reading is 1.22. A constant should be introduced here to renormalize the entire formula...

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: What the hell are you talking about?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'm laughing at you, Blake.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'm laughing at how pathetic you are. Your power, your medals, your rank in the DOD... You never lost sight of those.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: But now, we're standing at an altitude that few have ever touched, surrounded on all sides by scientific miracles. Just by reaching our hands out, we're on the cusp of plucking new formulae from these instruments.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Take a good look. Here, all the honors and accolades you've clung to are so small, so insignificant.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: And what about your Rhine Lab, Ferdinand?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Haven't you been fixated on that?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Let me make a correction. I've been fixated on what Rhine Lab represents.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Rhine Lab is my toolbox. My ladder, my arm. But it is not my purpose.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: In case you've forgotten, I can proudly proclaim that I am one of the finest high energy physicists in the land... No, in both the land and the skies.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What I've been fixated on has always been science itself.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Kristen, Kristen...

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: She created all of this, and let it go to waste. A truly prodigal genius she is.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And I envy her––

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: But I also have to admit, it's been an incredible ride.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And so, each and every second of my time is insanely valuable, and I can't afford to waste a moment on you.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Listen to me, Ferdinand. Don't forget who you take orders from, and who gave you your new lease on life!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Colonel, do you know how to stop a curious scientist?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You either satisfy him, or you kill him.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Get it over with. Don't waste time.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: One last thing I'd like to remind you of, soldiers.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The H.A.M.H.R.R. will crash after reactivation, taking all of us with it.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: All this data might mean nothing to you, but... your lives, I trust, are very important.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: If you want to know where the escape pods are, you shouldn't be in such a hurry.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: As for you, Blake, I'd save an extra bolt... Either for yourself, or the one you answer to. Doesn't matter to me.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Just, don't break my instruments.
